java-lab-1: Study a Java IDE such as Eclipse or NetBeans. Create a test project, add a class and run it. Explore suggestions, auto-fill, formatting and refactoring by renaming variables, methods and classes. Write a program to find prime numbers between 1 and n, then debug it step by step.
java-lab-2: Write a Java program that prints all real solutions of ax² + bx + c = 0. Read a, b and c from the user and use the quadratic formula.
java-lab-3: Write a Java program to multiply two given matrices.
java-lab-4: Write a Java program demonstrating inheritance, preventing inheritance using final, and abstract classes.
java-lab-5: Create an abstract class Shape containing two integers and an abstract printArea() method. Create Rectangle, Triangle and Circle subclasses. Each subclass must implement printArea() to print the area of its shape.
java-lab-6: Write a Java program to demonstrate method overloading and constructor overloading.
java-lab-7: Write a Java program to demonstrate method overriding.
java-lab-8: Write a Java currency converter using interfaces to convert Dollar, Euro and Yen amounts to INR.
java-lab-9: Write a Java program to demonstrate user-defined exception handling.
java-lab-10: Create a Java user interface for integer division with Num1, Num2 and Result text fields and a Divide button. Display Num1 divided by Num2 when the button is clicked. Handle non-integer input with NumberFormatException and a zero divisor with ArithmeticException. Display the exception in a message dialog.
java-lab-11: Write a Java application with three threads. The first generates a random integer every second. If it is even, the second thread prints its square; if it is odd, the third thread prints its cube.
java-lab-12: Write a Java program implementing the producer-consumer problem using inter-thread communication.
java-lab-13: Write a Java program to split a given text file into n parts. Name each part using the original filename followed by a .part suffix and its sequence number.
java-lab-14: Read a filename from the user. Display whether the file exists, whether it is readable or writable, its type, and its length in bytes.
java-lab-15: Write a Java program that connects to a database using JDBC and performs add, delete, modify and retrieve operations.
java-lab-16: Write a Java traffic-light simulation with radio buttons for Red, Yellow and Green. Selecting a light must show STOP, READY or GO above the buttons in the selected color. Initially, no message should be shown.
java-lab-17: Write a Java program that handles all mouse events using adapter classes. When an event occurs, display its name at the center of the window.
java-lab-18: Write a Java program to demonstrate key event handlers.
java-lab-19: Write a Java calculator using a grid layout for digit buttons and the +, -, *, and % operations, with a text field for the result. Handle possible exceptions, including division by zero.
java-lab-20: Develop a Java applet that displays a simple message.
java-lab-21: Develop a Java applet that accepts an integer in one text field and displays its factorial in another when the Compute button is clicked.
dbms-lab-1: Design an ER model for a college course-enrollment system. Identify Student, Course and Enrollment entities, their attributes and keys. Show relationship cardinalities and participation constraints, and explain your design.
dbms-lab-2: Convert a college course-enrollment ER model into relational tables. Define Student, Course and Enrollment with primary and foreign keys. Insert sample records and query the students enrolled in each course.
dbms-lab-3: Normalize Enrollment(roll_no, student_name, course_code, course_title, faculty_id, faculty_name, grade). Use roll_no → student_name; course_code → course_title, faculty_id; faculty_id → faculty_name; and (roll_no, course_code) → grade. Identify a candidate key, decompose to 3NF, create the resulting tables, and explain lossless decomposition and dependency preservation.
dbms-lab-4: Practice DDL by creating a Student table with suitable data types, a primary key, NOT NULL and CHECK constraints. Use ALTER TABLE to change its structure. Create and drop a separate practice table, then inspect the remaining schema.
dbms-lab-5: Practice DML on a Student table: insert sample rows, update a student's marks, delete a selected row, and retrieve the remaining records. Verify each change with a SELECT query.
dbms-lab-6: Using Student and Enrollment tables with sample data, write queries demonstrating ANY, ALL, IN, EXISTS, NOT EXISTS, UNION and INTERSECT. Define and test integrity constraints. Explain the result of each query.
dbms-lab-7: Create a student marks dataset. Write queries using aggregate functions, GROUP BY and HAVING to report departmental results. Create a view for high-scoring students, query it, and then drop it.
dbms-lab-8: Create INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE triggers on a Student table that record changes in an audit table. Perform all three operations and display the audit records to verify each trigger.
dbms-lab-9: Create a parameterized stored procedure to transfer an amount between two accounts. Validate the amount, account existence and available balance. Demonstrate successful and rejected calls and verify the final balances.
dbms-lab-10: Use an explicit cursor to read students and their marks in order. Open the cursor, fetch and process each row, terminate at the end and close it. Display the processed rows and count; compare with a set-based SELECT.
